title: Jared Kushner Is the Face of American Oligarchy
gist: This book excerpt argues that Jared Kushner's late-2025 Ukraine 'peace plan'—reportedly laundered almost word-for-word from a Kremlin document drafted by sanctioned insider Kirill Dmitriev—embodies an oligarchic capture of U.S. foreign policy that, by conceding a nuclear power's right to carve up a non-nuclear neighbor, risks igniting a new age of nuclear proliferation.

insights.claim: On Nov. 16, 2025, Jared Kushner presented Ukrainian President Zelensky a U.S.-approved list of demands requiring Ukraine to cap its military, abandon NATO membership, and cede all of Crimea and the Donbas—including territory Russia had never occupied—while Russia would see sanctions lifted.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: Terms conceding unconquered territory signal a U.S. negotiating posture maximally favorable to Moscow, a regime-shaping shift in the Ukraine war worth pricing into European risk.
insights.quote: Ukraine would have to finally, formally give up not just Crimea, but all of the Donbas—including territory that Russia hadn’t even occupied

insights.claim: Journalists Christo Grozev and Michael Weiss reported that Kushner's peace plan contained specific language appearing almost word-for-word in an earlier document drafted solely by sanctioned Kremlin insider Kirill Dmitriev, who reportedly said he would pass Moscow's document informally so Kushner and Witkoff could present it as their own.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: If a U.S. envoy is laundering Kremlin-drafted terms, U.S. mediation in Ukraine is compromised at the source—a credibility red flag for any settlement.
insights.quote: specific language that appeared almost exactly word-for-word in an earlier text—one drafted solely by Dmitriev
insights.locator: But as journalists Christo Grozev and Michael Weiss later revealed

insights.claim: In late October 2025, Kushner and Steve Witkoff met in Miami with Kirill Dmitriev—described as a sanctioned Kremlin insider tasked with recruiting Kushner to Moscow's side—before producing their 'original' points to resolve the Russia-Ukraine war.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: Documents a direct channel between U.S. negotiators and a sanctioned Kremlin operative, central to assessing the integrity of the peace process.
insights.quote: a sanctioned Kremlin insider tasked with recruiting Kushner to Moscow’s side
insights.locator: In late October 2025, Kushner and Witkoff huddled in Miami

insights.claim: The author frames Kushner as the consummation of oligarchy in Washington—an unelected billionaire subject to no oversight or disclosure requirements, present solely because of his relationship to his father-in-law, yet dominating U.S. policymaking.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: Personalized, unaccountable foreign-policymaking increases policy volatility and conflict-of-interest risk, a governance discount for U.S. institutional credibility.
insights.quote: an unelected billionaire, subject to no oversight or disclosure requirements, there solely because of his relationship with his father-in-law
insights.locator: It was a lesson that came straight from the mouth of a U.S. oligarch

insights.claim: Kushner's 2025 financial dealings included partnering with Saudi backers on the biggest leveraged buyout ever to acquire video-game maker Electronic Arts, a fast-tracked luxury real-estate development in Albania that sparked ongoing protests, and involvement in a Gaza ceasefire granting Israel occupation of most of the territory.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: The intertwining of Gulf-financed private deals with official diplomacy illustrates the conflict-of-interest surface around U.S. policy actors, relevant to EA and Saudi-linked assets.
insights.quote: he partnered with Saudi backers to launch the biggest leveraged buyout the world had ever seen, snapping up the video game company Electronic Arts

insights.claim: By pledging to recognize a nuclear power's right to carve up a non-nuclear neighbor, the Kushner plan establishes a new geopolitical principle that Russia's nuclear bluffing works—a lesson the author says will not be lost on non-nuclear states like Japan, South Korea, Poland, and Germany facing nuclear-armed rivals.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: If the takeaway is that nuclear weapons deter partition, expect renewed proliferation pressure among U.S. allies—a structural shift in global security and defense demand.
insights.quote: With Kushner’s plan, the United States was pledging to recognize a nuclear power’s right to carve up a non-nuclear neighbor.

insights.claim: The author predicts a forthcoming age of nuclear proliferation driven by Russia's imperialism, China's irredentism, and U.S. strategic myopia, with the rise of a self-serving U.S. oligarchy at the center of that story.
insights.speaker: Casey Michel
insights.so_what: A multi-cause proliferation thesis flags a decade-scale rise in nuclear-armed states, a tail risk for global stability and defense/security sectors.
insights.quote: when the story of this new surge of nuclear powers is written, there will be the rise of a U.S. oligarchy at the center
insights.locator: There are dozens of other factors
